cases.title: First lesson: asks what should snap before proposing; candidates as questions, at most three; real names

rubric.reason: Before any focus is proposed or anything is held, the mentor asks 'Is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?'; the short lead-in only names the candidates and sets no focus.

It names two candidates, Blink and Cut Opacity, and asks 'Should Blink or Cut snap instead of fading?'; 'both fade between their values' is neutral and is not called a mistake or an instruction to hold.
Blink (Opacity, from 1 s), Cut (Opacity, around 3 s) and the Seal precomp all match the snapshot's candidates (first_time 1 and 3) and left_out entries.

The mentor opens by explaining the lesson ("With hold, it waits and then jumps. With linear, it moves at a steady speed. With ease...") and listing the candidates before it asks "Is anything here meant to snap...", and the item says it must not start by explaining.

It names two candidates by layer and property (Blink and Cut, both Opacity, "right now they fade") and asks "Is either of these meant to snap instead of fading?", without calling either a mistake or telling the learner to hold.
Every name and time matches the snapshot result: Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity at 1 s with 3 pairs ("a few times"), Cut Opacity at 3 s with 1 pair ("once"), and Seal left out as a precomp.

The turn opens by explaining key types ('This lesson is about choosing each key's type on purpose... it can glide there (eased or linear), or it can wait and then jump') before any question, which the item forbids; it sets no focus, but the intent question only comes after the lead-in.

Two candidates (Blink's Opacity, Cut's Opacity) are named by layer and property and posed as a question ('Is either one meant to snap instead...? Or is a fade what you want'), with no fade called a mistake and no instruction to hold.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink Opacity at 1 s with three pairs, Cut Opacity at 3 s with one pair, and Seal left out as a precomp all match the key_types_snapshot result.
